correctness.rationale: Direct derivative confines stationary prices to (1/k,1); the logarithmic derivative of H has precisely the quadratic kp^2-(k+1)p+2, discriminant k^2-6k+1. Full signs and folds are proved analytically. The logarithmic revenue ratio at the two nondegenerate maxima has strictly positive envelope derivative in segment weight and opposite limiting signs, proving exactly one global optimizer switch. Critical and fold boundaries and parameter scaling explicitly checked. SymPy factorization plus 48 numerical parameter cases and k=10 double optimum replayed from delivered verify.py; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: A natural heterogeneous willingness-to-pay market can switch abruptly between low and high optimal uniform prices even as segment composition varies continuously. The complete sharp rate-contrast threshold, the precise two-local-maxima window, and exactly one global crossing supply parameter-wide structural insight and identify multiple local optimizer traps; this is not a single-exponential textbook optimum or a numerical special case. It provides a benchmark and conditioning boundary for segmentation and price fitting, without overclaiming policy implications beyond idealized model.
